parent_scope_objection: Second and final scoped scientific review, one prior scientific opinion retained in the attempt ceiling. Do not repair the legacy normalized/nonliteral quote or assume a technical inspector has decided correctness. Independent raw primary inspection raised this precise unresolved question: Legacy scientific decision and raw provider wording are preserved, but its nonliteral proof has not yet passed new literal-primary/context inspection. Abstract distinguishes nonsignificant Spanish independent sample from supportive pooled meta-analysis including previous data. The broad gene-risk conclusion is not an unqualified verdict on the independent retest. Read the full original-specific Results/Discussion/Conclusion, all earlier source/argument history and codebook. Settle the actual finding/type/identity and any dependent outcome using a short contiguous raw literal passage; distinct passages may be separately recorded, never spliced. The author whole-target synthesis governs over a secondary contrast, but generic theory or other-original support cannot be transferred. Same-source access is not identical sample/data; computational rerun, alternative-specification robustness and new-sample tests must remain separate. If there is an actual primary-source ambiguity or evidence-access limit, identify it exactly; no forced verdict. If original/type remains unresolved, do not transfer a categorical outcome. A removal needs positive target/duplicate evidence, never title/DOI difference alone.

prior_scientific_decisions.quote: By applying an allelic model, we observed a trend toward an association between this marker and late-onset AD susceptibility in our case–control study (odds ratio 5 1.114, 95% confidence interval: 0.958–1.296, P 5.16). Meta-analysis of available studies (n 5 31,771 individuals), including previous studies and public genome-wide association study resources (Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, Translational Genomics Research Institute, and Multi-site Collaborative Study for Genotype-Phenotype Associations in Alzheimer’s Disease), strongly supports the effect of rs3818361 (odds ratio 5 1.180, 95% confidence interval: 1.113–1.252, P , 2.99E-8) and suggests the existence of between-study heterogeneity (P , .05). We concluded that the complement receptor 1 gene may contribute to AD risk, although its effect size could be smaller than previously estimated.
prior_scientific_decisions.reason: Although the Spanish sample alone showed a nonsignificant trend (OR = 1.114, P = .16), the authors explicitly state that the observed effect size and direction were concordant with Lambert et al. [1] and conclude that CR1 contributes to AD risk with a smaller effect size; under the codebook, a weaker or nonsignificant effect treated by the authors as concordant with the original is coded as successful rather than mixed.
